newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Fletcher encounters gas in Brunei well.
newsitem.headline: Fletcher encounters gas in Brunei well.

text.p: Fletcher Challenge Energy said on Thursday it had encountered gas shows at its Perdana Deep-1 well in Brunei and it had also recorded improved gas flows at its Mangahewa-2 well in Taranaki on New Zealand's west Coast.

The size of the gas shows at Perdana were not detailed in a drilling report released by the company today which said only that the shows had been encountered in the MIO 100 sequence of the structure drilled.
The well has been drilled to a depth of 3631 metres.

Fletcher Energy owns 26.95 percent of the well after announcing recently that it had farmed out its interest to local and private investors. That farm-out is subject to the approval of the Brunei Government.
Perdana is considered a frontier exploration well into a structure that has been said to have the potential to hold between 500 million and one billion barrels of oil.
The company also announced that its Mangahewa-2 well onshore in Taranaki had flowed gas at a maximum rate of 1.5 million standard cubic feet with minor condensate and fluids also recorded.
This was an improved flow. That well was shut in on May 14 to permit perforation of the next zone. It is 100 percent-owned by Fletcher Challenge Energy.
